title: Full-measure of the good set $A$ ($|A|\sim S_3S_4$) via Sard for $p=(f_3,f_4)$ is invoked but not justified

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** §"The proof of the Proposition", definition of the good set
$$A=\{(a,b)\in[\tfrac14 S_3,\tfrac34 S_3]\times[\tfrac14 S_4,\tfrac34 S_4]: f\pitchfork\Sigma_{a,b}\},\qquad |A|\sim S_3 S_4.$$

**Gap.** The measure estimate $|A|\sim S_3 S_4$ is asserted via "By the transversality theorem, for almost every $(a,b)$ the map $f$ is transverse to $\Sigma_{a,b}$." This full-measure claim is load-bearing (it both makes $f^{-1}(\Sigma_{a,b})$ a submanifold and supplies the factor $|A|\sim S_3 S_4$ in the final averaging), but it is invoked in one line and not reduced to a precise theorem.

**What must be supplied.** Reduce to Sard for the piecewise-smooth map $p=(f_3,f_4):R\to[0,S_3]\times[0,S_4]$: a point $(a,b)$ is a regular value of $p$ **iff** $f$ is transverse to $\Sigma_{a,b}=\{y_3=a,y_4=b\}$ (since $\Sigma_{a,b}$ is the common level set of the last two coordinates and $f_1\in[0,S_1],f_2\in[0,S_2]$ always, so $f^{-1}(\Sigma_{a,b})=p^{-1}(a,b)$ — this set-equality is already proved later in the coarea step). By Sard's theorem (valid for piecewise-smooth / Lipschitz-with-a.e.-derivative maps in this dimension, or after smoothing on each piece) the regular values of $p$ have full measure in $[0,S_3]\times[0,S_4]$, so
$$|A|=\big|\{(a,b)\in[\tfrac14 S_3,\tfrac34 S_3]\times[\tfrac14 S_4,\tfrac34 S_4]: (a,b)\text{ regular for }p\}\big|=\tfrac14 S_3\cdot\tfrac14 S_4=\tfrac{1}{16}S_3 S_4,$$
hence $|A|\sim S_3 S_4$.

**Priority.** Low (P3): the underlying fact is standard, but as the file otherwise reproves standard lemmas in full, a one-line precise reduction to Sard via $p=(f_3,f_4)$ should be inserted. Not previously filed; complements prob-04-7 (coarea), which already establishes $f^{-1}(\Sigma_{a,b})=p^{-1}(a,b)$.
